claims.text: Greater overall social media use in adolescents is associated with poorer sleep quality.
Greater overall social media use in adolescents is associated with lower self-esteem.
Greater overall social media use in adolescents is associated with higher levels of anxiety and depression.
Nighttime-specific social media use predicts poorer sleep quality after controlling for anxiety, depression, and self-esteem.

evidence.description: Adolescents who used social media more - both overall and at night - and those who were more emotionally invested in social media experienced poorer sleep quality.
Adolescents who used social media more experienced lower self-esteem.
Adolescents who used social media more experienced higher levels of anxiety and depression.
Nighttime-specific social media use predicted poorer sleep quality after controlling for anxiety, depression and self-esteem.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional survey assessment
methodologies.description: Measured overall social media use, nighttime social media use, emotional investment, sleep quality, self-esteem, anxiety, and depression in 467 Scottish adolescents.
conditions: controlling for anxiety, depression and self-esteem

future_work.text: Further investigation into nighttime-specific social media use and emotional investment in social media in relation to adolescent sleep and wellbeing.
